dominant_strengths: Confident editorial typography with strong hierarchy: bold white headline against muted gray secondary copy creates clear reading rhythm
Restrained monochrome palette and consistent logo treatment in the customer strip feel premium and brand-cohesive
FIG 0.2/0.3/0.4 labels and isometric line illustrations add a technical, schematic craft signature distinct from generic SaaS
dominant_weaknesses: Three illustration tiles read as similar isometric stacks at similar weights, weakening visual differentiation between feature sections
Massive negative space between logo strip and headline feels like a scroll dead-zone rather than intentional pacing
Visual language closely mirrors current Linear/Vercel norms — competent but not breaking new ground in distinctiveness or innovation
fix_priorities: Differentiate the three FIG illustrations by motif, scale, or motion so each feature has a unique silhouette
Tighten vertical rhythm between sections; reduce empty band above the headline or fill it with a transitional element
Introduce a subtle accent (color, micro-interaction, or typographic flourish) to elevate distinctiveness above category baseline
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral polish and reflective brand signaling, but behavioral clarity is thin since the illustrations don't yet communicate distinct functions.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it executes the linear-scroll productivity-marketing pattern competently with editorial typography and schematic figures, though it leans heavily on category conventions.
